newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE, RANGERS, FLYERS REACH CONFERENCE FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE, RANGERS, FLYERS REACH CONFERENCE FINALS.

text.p: The NHL conference finals were set after the defending champion Colorado Avalanche, New York Rangers and Philadelphia Flyers all completed 4-1 series victories Sunday.
Adam Deadmarsh scored his second goal of the game, a power-play tally with 68 seconds remaining, as Colorado scored a 4-3 victory over the Edmonton Oilers.
The Rangers eliminated the New Jersey Devils with a 2-1 road victory on Adam Graves's goal 14:08 into overtime.

And in Buffalo, Eric Lindros scored twice in a 41-second span of the second period, including the first successful penalty shot in team playoff history, as the Flyers rolled to a 6-3 victory over the Sabres.
The Avalanche set up a rematch of last year's bitterly contested Western Conference finals with the Detroit Red Wings.

Deadmarsh outmuscled defenceman Luke Richardson in front of the net and Valeri Kamensky fed him a pass from behind the goal. Deadmarsh, who had not scored since Game 6 of the opening round, flicked a shot past goaltender Curtis Joseph's left skate for the game-winner.
"I hadn't done much before in this series," said Deadmarsh. "With Peter (Forsberg) out we needed to step up."

The goal turned Edmonton's Andrei Kovalenko from hero to goat. Kovalenko's power-play goal with 6:11 to play lifted the Oilers into a 3-3 tie. But he was penalised for cross-checking Mike Ricci with 2:20 left, providing Colorado's formidable power play with a chance to break the deadlock.

Claude Lemieux continued his postseason heroics for the Avalanche, scoring his 10th playoff goal 35 seconds into the third period to snap a 2-2 tie. Joseph made a pair of saves on Lemieux, who finally banked one off Richardson to extend his goal-scoring streak to seven games.
"The playoffs are my time, always have been," said Lemieux. "We know how to win the close games. Edmonton has a good young team, but they have to play in a few of these series to learn."
"Pepe (Lemieux) rose to the occasion as he always does at playoff time," said Colorado coach Marc Crawford.
Joe Sakic, the leading scorer in the postseason, and Deadmarsh gave Colorado a 2-0 lead with goals in the the first and second periods.

But Edmonton, appearing in the playoffs for the first time since 1992, rallied. Todd Marchant tied a postseason record with his third shorthanded goal, with 10:22 to go in the second period, and Jason Arnott got the tying goal just over eight minutes later.
New York eliminated New Jersey for the third time in six years, this time on a goal stunningly similar to the 1994 series-winner by Stephane Matteau over the Devils.

Mark Messier got the puck in his own zone and sent it ahead to Russ Courtnall. He got it down low to Graves, who shook off defenceman Scott Stevens, skated behind the net and beat Martin Brodeur on a wraparound between the pads.
"Mess made an outlet pass for us and I had momentum," Graves said. "I split the gap, just tried to get the puck and wrap it around. The puck had eyes, so to speak."
Like the double-overtime goal scored by Matteau in Game 7 of the 1994 Eastern finals, Brodeur unsuccessfully tried a pokecheck, leaving his pads wide open.
"It was pretty similar, a wraparound attempt to the same side. A pretty simple goal when you look at it," Messier said.

Esa Tikkanen scored his seventh goal of the playoffs 7:53 into the game to give the Rangers first blood for the fourth straight contest. "This is the time of year you want to play, and it feels great to be playing well," said Tikkanen.
Brian Rolston gave New Jersey its only goal on the power play at 12:20 of the second period.
New York goalie Mike Richter finished with 46 saves, including five in overtime, and had a spectacular .978 save percentage in the series.
In Buffalo, rookie Dainius Zubrus like Lindros had two goals for the Flyers, who advanced to the conference finals for the second time in three years.

"Our goal is not just to be in the third series, it's to win the third series," said Lindros. "When we are complete, we'll look further. The end of the tunnel is a long way away and we have to keep working toward it. Let's not get ahead of ourselves, but I feel real strong about our team."

The Flyers beat the Sabres for the fourth time in as many playoff meetings, preventing Buffalo from advancing to the third round for the first time since losing to Philadelphia in the 1975 Stanley Cup Finals.
Ron Hextall survived a shaky outing in his first appearance of the playoffs for the Flyers, who outshot Buffalo 40-24.

Buffalo goaltender Steve Shields, making his ninth straight start for the injured Dominik Hasek, stopped the first 22 shots before John LeClair tallied at 5:27 of the second period. Shjon Podein also tallied for Philadelphia..
Randy Burridge scored twice and Michal Grosek also tallied for the Sabres.
